```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

cases <- cases %>%
  mutate(Month = floor_date(as.Date(Date), unit = "month"))

monthly_counts <- cases %>%
  count(Month, name = "n") 

MonthlyModel <- glm(n ~ Month, data = monthly_counts)
summary(MonthlyModel)

ggplot(monthly_counts, aes(x = Month, y = n)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Cases Over Time (Linear Regression)",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Number of Cases"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

PMonthlyModel <- glm(n ~ Month, data = monthly_counts, family=poisson)
summary(PMonthlyModel)

monthly_counts$predicted <- predict(
  PMonthlyModel,
  newdata = monthly_counts,
  type = "response"
)

ggplot(monthly_counts, aes(x = Month, y = n)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = predicted),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Cases Over Time (Poisson Regression)",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Number of Cases"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


#Statistical Model
#model <- glm(n ~ Month, data = cases, family = poisson)
#summary(model)
#exp(coef(model))
```


```{r}
cases <- read_csv("data/hallucination_cases.csv")
knitr::kable(cases |> count(`Professional Sanction`, name = "Cases"))
model_data <- cases |>
  filter(`Professional Sanction` %in% c("No", "Yes")) |>
  transmute(
    sanction = factor(`Professional Sanction`, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
    party = case_when(
      str_detect(str_to_lower(coalesce(`Party(ies)`, "")), "lawyer|prosecutor|defender") ~ "Lawyer involved",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(coalesce(`Party(ies)`, "")), "pro se") ~ "Pro se litigant",
      is.na(`Party(ies)`) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ "Other party"),
    jurisdiction = case_when(`State(s)` == "USA" ~ "USA",
                             is.na(`State(s)`) ~ "Unknown", TRUE ~ "Outside USA"),
    tool = case_when(str_to_lower(`AI Tool`) == "chatgpt" ~ "ChatGPT",
                    str_to_lower(`AI Tool`) %in% c("implied", "unidentified") | is.na(`AI Tool`) ~ "Unspecified or implied",
                    TRUE ~ "Other named tool"),
    legal_field = coalesce(`Legal Field Primary`, "Unknown"))
sanction_rate <- mean(model_data$sanction == "Yes")
ggplot(model_data, aes(sanction)) + geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Recorded professional sanction", y = "Cases",
       title = "Professional sanctions are uncommon") + theme_minimal()
party_summary <- model_data |> group_by(party) |>
  summarise(Cases = n(), Yes = sum(sanction == "Yes"),
            Sanction_rate = mean(sanction == "Yes"), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(party_summary, digits = 3)
ggplot(party_summary, aes(reorder(party, Sanction_rate), Sanction_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") + coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Party category", y = "Proportion with sanction",
       title = "Recorded sanction rates by party type") + theme_minimal()
```

There are `r nrow(cases)` cases; `r nrow(cases) - nrow(model_data)` are
excluded for missing or unrecognized responses. Among retained cases,
`r round(100 * sanction_rate, 2)`% record a sanction. The imbalanced response
means high accuracy can conceal poor detection of Yes cases.
The party chart compares rates rather than counts to account for category
sizes. Lawyer involvement may be informative because professional discipline
applies to legal professionals. These associations do not establish causation.

## Shared modeling setup

```{r}
set.seed(154)
train_id <- sample(seq_len(nrow(model_data)), round(0.7 * nrow(model_data)))
train <- model_data[train_id, ]
test <- model_data[-train_id, ]
# Learn common fields from training data only; group unseen test levels.
common_fields <- train |> count(legal_field, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 8) |> pull(legal_field)
prepare_predictors <- function(d) {
  d |> mutate(
    legal_field = factor(ifelse(legal_field %in% common_fields, legal_field, "Other"),
                         levels = c(common_fields, "Other")),
    party = factor(party, levels = c("Lawyer involved", "Pro se litigant", "Other party", "Unknown")),
    jurisdiction = factor(jurisdiction, levels = c("USA", "Outside USA", "Unknown")),
    tool = factor(tool, levels = c("ChatGPT", "Unspecified or implied", "Other named tool")))
}
train <- prepare_predictors(train)
test <- prepare_predictors(test)
model_formula <- sanction ~ party + jurisdiction + tool + legal_field
knitr::kable(data.frame(Set = c("Training", "Test"),
                       Cases = c(nrow(train), nrow(test)),
                       Yes_rate = c(mean(train$sanction == "Yes"), mean(test$sanction == "Yes"))), digits = 3)
```
